question.problem: Find the disjoint union of the sets ${A}_{1}=\{-2,\pi \}$ and ${A}_{2}=\{\pi ,4\}.$
question.worked_solution:
Notice that the sets are overlapping since

$$
\{-2,\pi \}\cap \{\pi ,4\}=\{\pi \}\ne ∅.
$$

So, for each of our sets, we form the associated set, where each element is tagged with the corresponding index, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & {A}_{1} &  & \,\to \, &  & {A}_{1}^{∗}=\{(-2,1),(\pi ,1)\} \\  & {A}_{2} &  & \,\to \, &  & {A}_{2}^{∗}=\{(\pi ,2),(4,2)\}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the disjoint union of our sets is simply the union of the associated tagged sets:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1}⊔{A}_{2} & =\{-2,\pi \}⊔\{\pi ,4\} \\  & ={A}_{1}^{∗}\cup {A}_{2}^{∗} \\  & =\{(-2,1),(\pi ,1)\}\cup \{(\pi ,2),(4,2)\} \\  & =\{(-2,1),(\pi ,1),(\pi ,2),(4,2)\}\end{aligned}
$$
